{{Short description|On when a smooth map between smooth manifolds is a locally trivial fibration}}
In [[mathematics]], or specifically, in [[differential topology]], '''Ehresmann's lemma''' or '''Ehresmann's fibration theorem''' states that if a [[smooth mapping]] <math> f\colon M \rightarrow N</math>, where <math> M </math> and <math>N</math> are [[smooth manifold]]s, is
# a surjective [[submersion (mathematics)|submersion]], and
# a [[proper map]] (in particular, this condition is always satisfied if ''M'' is [[Compact space|compact]]),

then it is a [[locally trivial]] [[fibration]]. This is a foundational result in [[differential topology]] due to [[Charles Ehresmann]], and has many variants.
